kill_fact: All three kill conditions hold, each verified independently against a primary source, and the verdict survives every correction credited in the BULL's favour. (1) THE CATALYST IS NOT LIVE, DATED OR BINDING. The 2025-12-09 announcement forming the Special Committee (J.P. Morgan financial advisor, Wachtell Lipton counsel) states verbatim: 'There can be no assurance that the Special Committee's review process will result in any particular outcome or transaction, and there is no definitive timeline set for the completion of the review process,' adding the company will not update 'until it determines that additional disclosure is appropriate or necessary.' The SEC filing record through 2026-07-17 contains NO merger 8-K, NO definitive agreement and NO DEFM14A -- eleven months after J.P. Morgan was retained there is no buyer, no price, no outside date and no vote. Worse, the company has verbally downgraded its own catalyst: on the 2026-05-11 Q1 call interim CEO Nancy Curtin said, in unscripted Q&A, 'we are very laser-focused on really just evaluating opportunities that come, as opposed to a strategic review process in place at the moment' -- the formal sale process is not running -- while CFO Michael Harrington guided review costs off ('when we get in the back half of this year, that should be behind us'). Advisory fees are the truest instrument for whether a banker is still working, and they are being guided down. The 2026-06-17 annual meeting, the natural forcing window, passed uncontested (all seven directors elected, KPMG ratified). (2) THE ENTRY PREMISE IS VOID. The board tagged this 'Forced_divest_flow.' There is no forced seller. The only verified supply is a Form S-3 (filed 2026-06-30, EFFECT 2026-07-10) registering 3,053,263 Class A shares -- 2.76% of the 110,744,073.25 Class A outstanding at 2026-06-18 -- for holders of April 6, 2023 Alvarium acquisition consideration. That is earn-out housekeeping that ADDS supply. The largest holder is the opposite of a forced seller: Allianz is a would-be acquirer, standstill-bound to the later of 2027-07-31, and ACCUMULATING -- a Form 4 dated 2026-07-02 shows it took 1,272,328.52 Class A shares plus 4,117.76 Series A preferred shares as PIK dividends. The only hard dates (Series A transfer restriction lapsing 2026-07-31; a 30% step-down in Allianz's common lock-up the same date) are permissions to sell, not clearing events. There is no overhang to clear and no washout to buy. (3) NO FLOOR AND THE SPREAD IS INVERTED. Nothing contractual, tangible or earnings-based backstops $3.58: there are no signed terms, hence no deal-break price; tangible common equity is negative (corrected to roughly -$197M, see corrections); the $2.75 52-week low is a chart marker, not a backstop. Press reporting confirms a $600M+ gap because buyers price BELOW the tape -- so a sale is a source of downward price discovery, not upside. Even after crediting every correction in the bull's favour (net cash, not net debt), a base-case 12.5x on $59M normalized adjusted EBITDA reconciles to roughly $2.71/sh against $3.58 live: the common still clears BELOW the tape on a rational buyer's multiple. And time is the adversary -- $352.209M of preferred compounding at 9.75% accreted $339.717M -> $345.838M -> $352.209M across the last three quarters (~$6.25M/qtr, ~$25M/yr on the balance, ~$34M/yr full economic cost) and settles part of itself in newly issued stock at multi-year lows, into a thin float. The asymmetry does not survive: soft decaying catalyst, void premise, no verified floor, inverted spread. Revisit only on a signed agreement with disclosed terms that clears the $352M preferred with room to spare.
corrections: The PASS/REFUTED conclusion survives intact, but two load-bearing anchors in the dossier are WRONG and both err AGAINST the common -- the negative asymmetry is real but materially thinner than the file claims. This shard supersedes and merges a prior pass; where the two disagreed I re-derived from the 2026-03-31 10-Q and adjudicate below. (a) MATERIAL -- TANGIBLE COMMON EQUITY OF -$550M DOUBLE-COUNTS THE PREFERRED. The preferred is MEZZANINE equity, presented OUTSIDE permanent equity. This is arithmetically provable from the filing: total stockholders' equity $618.714M + non-controlling interest $263.810M = $882.524M total equity exactly -- the $352.209M preferred is NOT inside that sum. The dossier subtracts it again. Correct TCE = $618.714M - $815.904M goodwill+intangibles = roughly -$197.2M, not -$550M. Still negative, so the NO-FLOOR finding stands, but the file overstates it ~2.8x. (b) MATERIAL -- THE NET DEBT / NET CASH TREATMENT. The file's '$77.2M total debt / $37.5M net debt' ties to the standard data-vendor convention but is an aggregation that INCLUDES $54.428M of capital lease obligations; the reported borrowings are $6.353M current + $16.459M non-current = $22.812M, and the company's own Q1 8-K reports total debt of $15.0M net of unamortized deferred financing costs (mainly a noninterest-bearing settlement loan tied to the DISCONTINUED International Real Estate business). Ex-leases the company is NET CASH (roughly $16.9M to $24.7M depending on convention), not $37.5M net debt -- a ~$54-62M / ~$0.36-0.42-per-share swing that lifts every SoP figure: base 12.5x/$59M goes $2.34 -> ~$2.71; the strategic 16x case rises above the file's $4.40; the adverse case rises above $0.88. Fair value moves from ~$2.85 toward ~$3.10-3.25 and risk/reward improves from ~0.65:1 toward ~0.85:1. STILL negative, STILL below the $3.58 tape -- the verdict does not flip -- but the margin is narrower than stated. Note the file's convention is also internally inconsistent: adjusted EBITDA is struck AFTER rent expense, so adding the lease liability to the EV bridge double-counts the leases. (c) MINOR -- SERIES A FACE IS UNDERSTATED. The file states Series A face of $140M and total preferred face of $290M. Allianz's 13D/A confirms 140,000 Series A shares at issuance PLUS an additional 18,471 purchased 2025-05-13, and PIK accretion carried the balance to 173,051.67 shares (~$173.05M at the $1,000 liquidation preference) as of 2026-07-02 -- so the file's own in-dossier 'correction' to $290M face is itself incomplete. Immaterial ONLY because the math correctly runs off the confirmed $352.209M CARRYING value, not face; and with the Series A conversion price at $8.70 (far out of the money at $3.58) the holder takes the preference rather than converting, so subtracting carrying value is the right treatment. (d) MINOR -- Allianz holds 24.86% of Class A (26,707,213.96 shares at 2026-03-31), not the file's 'about 26%,' consistent with the 24.9% cap the file cites elsewhere. (e) MINOR -- press accounts describe Tiedemann's 2026-03-30 exit variously as terminated 'without cause' and as a 'voluntary departure without cause'; 'ousted' is a characterization, not a verified fact. The file's rendering of the bidder complaint ('a mathematical disparity between what a sponsor would pay...') is a paraphrase of sourced wording ('the seller places a premium value on the AuM and revenues, but buyers may feel the cost of generating that revenue doesn't support the asking price') -- directionally identical, but a paraphrase, not a quote. ADJUDICATING THE PRIOR PASS, which erred on three points: its doubt that the Curtin quote came from the 2026-05-11 call is WRONG -- 'as opposed to a strategic review process in place at the moment' is confirmed verbatim in the Q1 2026 (11 May 2026) transcript across two independent renderings; its 'NOT VERIFIED' flag on Tiedemann's 9.8% stake and take-private 13D is resolved -- press reporting confirms both (13D, 9.8%, may submit proposals for extraordinary corporate transactions); and its PIK-accretion critique ('$48M/yr overstated') attacked an older data series -- the file's ~$6.25M/qtr / ~$25M/yr balance accretion is CONFIRMED exactly by the 10-Q sequence. VERIFIED AS STATED, tying exactly to the 2026-03-31 10-Q and the live quote: preferred carrying $352.209M; cash $39.715M; goodwill $384.586M + intangibles $431.318M = $815.904M on total assets $1,138.216M (~72% acquisition accounting); retained earnings -$410.311M; revenue $73.1M +28%; adj. EBITDA $14.9M +21% at a 20% margin vs 13%; AUM $48.7B / AUA $90.1B; net client outflows -$0.2B; live price $3.58 with a $2.75 52-week low and $3.92 200-day. Also note Q1 2026 net income from continuing operations was POSITIVE $8.4M (+$7.7M attributable), so the file's 'adjusted EBITDA does not survive to the bottom line' is true on a TTM basis but not for the latest print -- and the TTM loss is dominated by the now-discontinued International Real Estate operations, overstating the forward entity's burn.
